MINUTES
  Regular Meeting Notice of the
  Gardena City Council
  Tuesday, June 28, 2022

In order to minimize the spread of the COVID 19 virus, Governor Newsom has signed Assembly
Bill 361. Please be advised that the Council Chambers are closed to the public and that some,
or all, of the Gardena City Council Members may attend this meeting telephonically.

The Regular Meeting Notice and Agenda of the Gardena City Council of the City of Gardena,
California, was called to order at 7:02 PM on Tuesday, June 28, 2022, Mayor Tasha Cerda
presiding.

1.  ROLL CALL

  Present: Mayor Pro Tem Rodney G. Tanaka; Council Member Mark E. Henderson; Council
  Member Art Kaskanian; and Council Member Paulette C. Francis; Other City Officials and
  Employees present: City Manager Clint Osorio; City Attorney Carmen Vasquez; and City
  Clerk Mina Semenza. Mayor Pro Tem started the meeting as Mayor Cerda was running
  late but was on her way.

  At 7:03 p.m., the City Council recessed into Closed Session via Microsoft Teams, with the
  following in attendance: Mayor Tasha Cerda; Mayor Pro Tem Rodney G. Tanaka; Council
  Member Mark E. Henderson; Council Member Art Kaskanian; Council Member Paulette C.
  Francis. Other City Officials and Employees present: City Manager Clint Osorio; City
  Attorney Carmen Vasquez; and Director of Administrative Services Ray Beeman.

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION - None

2.  CLOSED SESSION

  2.A  CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATORS
  Government Code Section 54957.6
  Agency Designated Representative: Clint Osorio, City Manager
  Employee Organizations:
  1. Gardena Police Officers Association (GPOA), Matt Hassoldt,
  Association President
  2. Gardena Management Employees Organization (GMEO), Vicky L. Barker,
  Attorney
  3. Gardena Municipal Employees Association (GMEA), Fred G. Quiel, Attorney
  4. Confidential / Unrepresented Employees

  2.B  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL- EXISTING LITIGATION
  Gov. Code Section 54956.9(d)(1)
  Kenneth Miller vs. City of Gardena
  WCAB No.: ADJ11017715 and Judicate West Case No. A288686.

  Mayor Cerda reconvened the meeting to the Regular Open Session at
  7:49p.m., and the City Clerk noted the return of all Council Members, who
  were present at the meeting. When City Attorney Vasquez was asked if there
  was any reportable action from Closed Session, she stated for the record

  1
   that Mayor Cerda arrived at 7:11p.m. and was present for both items; she
  then continued to say that staff was provided with direction, but no
  reportable action had been taken.

3.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Kyle Vault was not available to do the Pledge; Council Member Art Kaskanian led the
  Pledge of Allegiance.

4.  INVOCATION

  Presented by Mayor Pro Tem Rodney G. Tanaka

5.  PRESENTATIONS

  5.A Boards & Commissions Update - Human Services Commission
  - Chair, LaWanda Staten provided the update and video presentation. Liaison,
  Dianna Espinoza was present and assisted with the presentation.

  5.B National Mosquito Control Awareness Week
  - Director of Communications of GLA County Vector Control District, Mary-Joy
  Coburn gave a presentation.

  5.C SB 1383 Mandatory Organics Recycling
  - Waste Resources Representative, Michelle Nicholls gave a presentation.

  HF&H Consultant Debbie Morris, WRG Representative Bevan Thomas and Program
  Coordinator of Public Works, Hong Lee were present and available for any questions.

  Council Member Francis thanked Ms. Nicholls for the presentation and mentioned that
  the City of Los Angeles and other cities are getting separate containers to their
  residents for their organics; and asked why we aren’t being provided the same service;
  she continued to say that her green container is full of all the greens from her garden;
  she also said that her sister has one, it’s a smaller container for just organic waste.

  Mayor Cerda asked about the people who are mulching food and turning it into
  compost is that defeating the purpose because this is the process WRG will be
  implementing; are residents getting violations for throwing away things that they could
  sell or donate? Mayor Cerda stated that everyone would need to participate starting
  on July 1st.

  Council Member Kaskanian thanked Ms. Nicholls for her presentation; he then asked
  about commercial clients and restaurants and how they are going to separate their
  organic waste. He then asked if it was if it applied to all commercial.

  Ms. Nicholls, Mr. Thomas and Ms. Morris answered all of Council’s questions.

  5.D Certificate of Recognition to Carlos Lifosjoe in appreciation of his service to the
  community as a Member of the Gardena Economic Business Advisory Commission
  - Item tabled to a later date.

  5.E Presentation of the Business Welcome Packet

  2
   - Economic Development Manager, Jackie Choi gave a presentation and
  explained the contents of the Business Welcome Packet.

  Council Member Kaskanian thanked, Ms. Choi for the great presentation and asked;
  have we done something like this previously?

  Mayor Cerda commented that she remembers that PD did a welcome packet.

  Ms. Choi replied that she has not seen anything printed from our division.

  City Manager Osorio added, no this has never been done before, and thanked Jackie
  for the presentation.

6.  PROCLAMATIONS - None

7.  APPOINTMENTS

  7.A  Council Appointments to Commissions, Committees, Councils and
  Boards (Appointees to be Ratified and Sworn In)

  Gardena Economic Business Advisory Commission - Joshua Bettencourt
  - was Appointed by City Manager Clint Osorio

  City Manager Osorio explained that Carlos Lifsojoe resigned from his position.

  It was moved by Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka, seconded by Council Member
  Kaskanian, and carried by the following roll call vote to Appoint Joshua
  Bettencourt to the Gardena Economic Business Advisory Commission:

  Ayes:  Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka, Council Members Kaskanian, Henderson and
  Francis, and Mayor Cerda
  Noes: None
  Absent: None

8.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  8.A  Approve Minutes:
  Regular Meeting of the City Council, June 14, 2022
  CONTACT: CITY CLERK

  8.B  Receive and File of Minutes:

  CONTACT: COMMUNITY DEVLEOPMENT

  8.C  Approval of Warrants/Payroll Register, June 28, 2022

  167782 -167984 – for a total Warrants issued in the amount of $2,678,229.00 Total
  Payroll Issued for June 17, 2022: $2,050,719.39.

  3
 8.D  Monthly Investment Portfolio, May 2022
  CONTACT: CITY TREASURER

8.E  Personnel Report P-2022-12 6-28-22
  CONTACT: HUMAN RESOURCES

  declared the Existence of a Local Emergency
  CONTACT: CITY MANAGER

  RESOLUTION NO. 6590

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  GARDENA, CALIFORNIA, REAFFIRMING PROCLAMATION AND
  RESOLUTION 6441 WHICH DECLARED THE EXISTENCE OF A
  LOCAL EMERGENCY

8.G  RESOLUTION NO. 6591, Making the legally required findings to Re-Authorize the
  use of Teleconferencing in accordance with Assembly Bill 361 for meetings of the

  State open meeting laws.
  CONTACT: CITY MANAGER

  RESOLUTION NO. 6591

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF

  FINDINGS  TO  RE-AUTHORIZE  THE  USE  OF
  TELECONFERENCING IN ACCORDANCE WITH ASSEMBLY BILL
  361 FOR MEETINGS OF THE GARDENA CITY COUNCIL AND

  County Metropolitan Transportation Authority for the Transit Oriented Communities

  to execute Right-of-Way Certifications and to sign Federal-Aid funding documents

  CONTACT: PUBLIC WORKS

   RESOLUTION NO. 6569

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  GARDENA, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING AND AUTHORIZING THE
  DIRECTOR OF PUBLIC WORKS OR CITY ENGINEER TO
  EXECUTE RIGHT OF WAY CERTIFCATIONS AND TO SIGN

  CONTACT: PUBLIC WORKS

  It was moved by Council Member Henderson, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem
  Tanaka, and carried by the following roll call vote to Approve all Items on the
  Consent Calendar with the exception of Items 8.H and 8.J:

  Ayes:  Council Member Henderson, Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka, Council
  Members Kaskanian and Francis, and Mayor Cerda
  Noes: None
  Absent: None

9.  EXCLUDED CONSENT CALENDAR

  8.H  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT - Authorizing the City Manager to Approve the Award
  Agreement with the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority for the
  Transit Oriented Communities Technical Assistance Program
  - This Item was pulled by Council Member Francis

  Council Members Francis asked if there’s money attached to this; she asked about
  the technical assistance and if we’ve been designated as a transit-oriented
  community; and asked which area this would take place at; she then asked about
  objective standards and who gets a copy of the final report.

  Council Member Henderson will we be able to increase the amount once the
  development goes up on El Segundo and Crenshaw?

  Council Member Kaskanian asked how much money can be requested for this grant;
  he then asked how much did we spend?

  City Manager Osorio and Director of Community Development Greg Tsujiuchi came
  into the meeting and answered Council Member Francis’ questions.

  8.J  PUBLIC WORKS - RESOLUTION NO. 6569, Authorizing the Director of Public Works
  or City Engineer to execute Right-of-Way Certifications and to sign Federal-Aid
  funding documents associated with grant funding allocations pursuant to Master
  Agreement No. 07-5276F15 between the City of Gardena and the State of California.
  - This Item was pulled by Council Member Francis

  5
   Council Member Francis asked if there is money tied to this project and how much
  are we receiving; she then asked about the executing of Right of Way Certifications?

  City Manager Osorio and Director of Public Works, Allan Rigg were available and
  answered all of Council Member Francis’ questions.

  It was moved by Council Member Francis, seconded by Council Member
  Henderson, and carried by the following roll call vote to Approve Items 8.H and
  8.J:

  Ayes:  Council Members Francis and Henderson, Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka,
  Council Member Kaskanian, and Mayor Cerda
  Noes: None
  Absent: None

10. PLANNING & ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY COMMISSION ACTION SHEET

  10.A  JUNE 21, 2022 MEETING
  Conditional Use Permit #4-22
  The Planning Commission considered a request for a conditional use permit to allow
  the use of an adult day care facility within an existing medical and professional office
  building located in the General Commercial (C-3) zone, which qualified for an
  exemption from CEQA as an existing facility. APPLICANT: David Kim
  LOCATION: 1045 Redondo Beach Boulevard

  Commission Action: The Planning Commission approved Resolution No. PC 9-
  22, approving Conditional Use Permit #4-22 subject to the attached Conditions of
  Approval and directing staff to file a Notice of Exemption.

  City Council Action: Receive and file or Call for Review (By way of two votes
  from the City Council)

  Council Member Francis called for review – no second.

  This Item was Received and Filed

  10.B  JUNE 21, 2022 MEETING
  ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT #5-21, ZONE TEXT AMENDMENT #2-21,
  ZONE CHANGE #1-21, CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT #1-21, SITE PLAN #3-21
  The Planning Commission considered the following for the redevelopment of an
  existing U -Haul facility on a 4.2 acre site: ZTA #2-21 to amend the Gardena
  Municipal Code Section 18.34.030, to allow for greater ground floor street frontage
  for self-storage facilities in the Heavy Commercial (C -4) zone; ZC #1-21 to change
  the current zone of General Commercial (C-3) with a Mixed-Use Overlay (MUO) to
  C -4 with an MUO; CUP #1-21 to allow the use of a self-storage facility within the
  C-4 zone; SPR #3-21 to approve the proposed site plan to develop a new 177,573
  gross square foot, five-story self-storage facility to the northern portion of the site
  and a separate 8,000 square-foot single-story building for retail sales and office use
  within the southern portion; and adopt Mitigated Negative Declaration (MND) and
  Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program (MMRP) (EA #5-21). APPLICANT:
  AMERCO Real Estate Company/U-Haul LOCATION: 14206 Van Ness Avenue

  6
   Commission Action: The Planning Commission continued the item to a future
  meeting, which will be re-noticed in the Gardena Valley News and new mailers will
  be sent to all properties within a 300-foot radius of the project site.

  City Council Action: No action required.

  This item was tabled to a future meeting - City Attorney Vasquez informed
  everyone that this item has not been continued to a set date of the PEQC.

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

1) City Clerk Mina Semenza, noted for the record the email received by a member of the public
  and that it has been forwarded to the City Council.

11. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES

  11.A PUBLIC HEARING: RESOLUTION NO. 6589, Adopting the City of Gardena's Two-
  Year Budget for Fiscal Years 2022-2023 And 2023-2024

  RESOLUTION NO. 6589

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  GARDENA, CALIFORNIA, ADOPTING A BUDGET FOR SAID CITY
  FOR THE FISCAL YEARS JULY 1, 2022, TO AND INCLUDING
  JUNE 30, 2023, AND JULY 1, 2023, TO AND INCLUDING JUNE 30,
  2024

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report and Power Point Presentation.

  Director of Administrative Services, Ray Beeman was available for any questions.

  Mayor Cerda opened the Public Hearing at 9:18 p.m. and asked if there were any
  comments from the public.

  Council Member Francis thanked City Manager Osorio for the presentation and asked
  what it means if a budget is structurally balanced, and the 40% reserve is that unusual
  for a city of our size, are we a lean budget; how has the budget so prepared us so
  that we will be able to survive a recession?

  Council Member Henderson thanked City Manager Osorio for the report and
  acknowledged that now we are at a modest rate; if we get a large liability; what does
  that look like to our financial reputation with our bonds, and what does that do to our
  bond rating?

  City Manager Osorio answered all of Council Members Francis and Henderson’s
  questions.

  No Public Speakers.

  There was no further comment, Mayor Cerda closed the Public Hearing at 9:27 p.m.

  7
   It was moved by Council Member Henderson, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem
  Tanaka, and carried by the following roll call vote to Conduct Public Hearing
  and Adopt Budget Resolution No. 6589:

  Ayes:  Council Member Henderson, Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka, Council
  Members Kaskanian and Francis, and Mayor Cerda
  Noes: None
  Absent: None

11.B RESOLUTION NO. 6588, Acknowledging the Receipt and Filing of the Annual
  Statement of Investment Policy for the Fiscal Year 2022-2023

  RESOLUTION NO. 6588

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  GARDENA, CALIFORNIA, ACKNOWLEDGING THE RECEIPT AND
  FILING OF THE ANNUAL STATEMENT OF INVESTMENT POLICY
  FOR THE FISCAL YEAR 2022-2023

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  It was moved by Council Member Francis, seconded by Council Member
  Kaskanian, and carried by the following roll call vote to Adopt Resolution No.
  6588:

  Ayes: Council Members Francis and Kaskanian, Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka,
  Council Member Henderson, and Mayor Cerda
  Noes: None
  Absent: None

11.C RESOLUTION NO. 6587, Establishing the Appropriations Limit for Fiscal Year
  2022-2023 (GANN Limit)

  RESOLUTION NO. 6587

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  GARDENA,  CALIFORNIA,  ESTABLISHING  ITS
  APPROPRIATIONS LIMIT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2022-2023 (GANN
  Limit)

  City Manager Osorio presented the Staff Report.

  Mayor Cerda opened the Public Hearing at 9:32 p.m. and asked if there were any
  comments from the public.

  Council Member Francis asked if the City Manager could explain in layman’s terms
  does this mean we can’t spend more than $132 million.

  City Manager Osorio answered Council Member Francis’ question.

  No Public Speakers.
  8
   There was no further comment, Mayor Cerda closed the Public Hearing at 9:34 p.m.

  It was moved by Council Member Henderson, seconded by Council Member
  Francis, and carried by the following roll call vote to Conduct Public Hearing
  and Adopt Resolution No. 6587 which establishes the City's Appropriations
  Limit for Fiscal Year 2022-2023 at $132,903,741 as required by Article XII (B) of
  the California Constitution:

  Ayes:  Council Members Henderson and Francis, Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka,
  Council Member Kaskanian, and Mayor Cerda
  Noes:  None
  Absent: None

  11.D Authorization to Bind Excess Insurance Coverage Policies for Fiscal Year 2022-
  2023

  City Manager Osorio presented Staff Report.

  Council Member Francis asked if these are companies we have used before and if our
  childcare network is covered as well; and then confirmed this is for city employees
  only.

  City Manager Osorio and City Attorney Vasquez answered all of Council Member
  Francis’ questions

  It was moved by Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka, seconded by Council Member
  Henderson, and carried by the following roll call vote to Authorize City Manager
  to Purchase and Bind Excess Insurance Coverage:

  Ayes:  Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka, Council Members Henderson, Kaskanian and
  Francis, and Mayor Cerda
  Noes:  None
  Absent: None

12. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT – No Items

13. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - ELECTED & CITY MANAGER'S OFFICES

  13.A COVID-19 Update

  City Manager Osorio presented the update.

  13.B First Amendment to City Manager Employment Agreement and RESOLUTION NO.
  6592, Adopting the City of Gardena Classification and Compensation Plan, effective
  June 28, 2022.

  9
   RESOLUTION NO. 6592

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  GARDENA, CALIFORNIA, ADOPTING CITY OF GARDENA
  CLASSIFICATION AND COMPENSATION PLAN, EFFECTIVE
  JUNE 28, 2022

  City Attorney Vasquez presented the Staff Report.

  Council Member Henderson thanked City Manager Osorio for his work in getting us
  through COVID, structure liability a good fiduciary steward especially navigating thru
  COVID.

  Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka added, I think we all owe the City Manager Osorio a lot of
  gratitude to go from 2019 with no benefit raise until now and work as hard and
  diligently as has; we all thank you for what you’ve done.

  Council Member Kaskanian echoed his colleagues: Clint a job well done we have the
  proof in front of us the city has 45%; the most difficult thing we did going thru COVID;
  we do need a person like you in the city who is good with the numbers, I commend
  you a job well done. You deserve everything.

  Council Member Francis thanked City Manager Osorio for all he has done for the City
  of Gardena; it’s 5% per year or one time 5%; City Attorney Vasquez confirmed it was
  a one time; Council Member Francis commented that she did her research, and we
  are comparable to other cities when it comes to City Manager’s. servant’s pay: I think
  you have saved us that much than what we are contributing towards your salary.

  Mayor Cerda congratulated him on a job well done.

  City Manager Osorio spoke and thanked everyone.

  It was moved by Mayor Cerda, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka, and carried
  by the following roll call vote to Approve the First Amendment to the City
  Manager Employment Agreement and Adopt Resolution No. 6592:

  Ayes:  Mayor Cerda, Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka, and Council Members
  Henderson, Kaskanian, and Francis
  Noes: None
  Absent: None

14. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS – POLICE – No Items

15. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - PUBLIC WORKS – No Items

16. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS - RECREATION & HUMAN SERVICES – No Items

17. DEPARTMENTAL ITEMS – TRANSPORTATION – No Items

18. COUNCIL ITEMS – No Items

  10
 19. COUNCIL DIRECTIVES

  Council Member Henderson

  1. Asked for an update on the park electric signs. Council Member Kaskanian seconded it.

  2. Asked when can we start working on the Environmental Justice Electric Dashboard to
  track the progress as we start addressing issues. Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka seconded it.

  Council Member Kaskanian

  1. He experienced multiple vehicles making a left turn onto the eastbound on Rosecrans
  because of the street modification made by the G3 Urban project located at Rosecrans
  Ave. He is asking for someone to look into it because he considers it to be a liability.
  Council Member Henderson seconded it.

  Council Member Francis

  1. Since we are in a drought, she asked for an update on the improvements for our park
  lands and cityscape from Director of Public Works, Allan Riggs. She also commented
  on the electrical park signs. City Manager Osorio replied that a second will not be
  required, and an update will be provided.

  Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka

  1. Asked if Public Works can contact WRG about the huge dumpster at Albertsons that is
  covered in graffiti and have it replaced. Mayor Cerda stated we do not have to make it a
  directive just report it on Gardena Direct.

  • Juneteenth – Acknowledge/Educate/Celebrate, Saturday, June 18, 2022, 2:00 p.m. –

21. COUNCIL REMARKS

  1. Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka – Since the last meeting Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka attended the
  South Bay Association of Realtors breakfast. Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka apologized for not
  attending the Juneteenth event as he had Father’s Day weekend planned at Palm
  Dessert. He also attended the COG Board of Directors meeting was elected second vice
  chair for the COG, burial ceremony of Ted Roy, and West Basin Water inauguration of
  their spiral filler with Council Member Henderson. Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka complimented
  Chief Saffell and departments for their work, urged everyone to use Gardena Direct and
  calling the non-emergency number to report illegal fireworks. Wished everyone a happy
  4th of July.
  2. Council Member Kaskanian – Council Member Kaskanian didn’t have much to report. He
  did apologize for not attending the Juneteenth event as he was out of town. Thanked
  Chief Saffell for the presentation and information. Wished everyone a happy 4 th of July
  and asked everyone to keep Gardena moving forward.
  3. Council Member Henderson – Council Member Henderson started off commenting and
  gave some gratitude to city staff and to the department heads as they are doing a great
  job. Complimented every department in the city. Since the last meeting Council Member
  Henderson attended the AQMD meeting, Juneteenth celebration, was interviewed on
  KBLA 1580. He also wished his son Mark Henderson II a happy 30th birthday. He also
  attended the Bizfed meeting, Executive board meeting, Responsible Governance
  Committee, and spoke during the homeownership fair with the consolidated board of
  realtors. Lastly, he celebrated his wedding anniversary with Michelle Henderson.

  12
   4. Mayor Cerda – Since the last meeting Mayor Cerda attended the South Bay Association
  of Realtors breakfast thanked City Clerk Mina for the hard work relators do and thanked
  all realtors. She was the keynote speaker at Environmental Charter High School
  commencement. Mayor Cerda also attended the Juneteenth celebration, Liberty
  Tabernacle church supported their Father’s Day event, spoke at the retirement of the first
  African American Battalion Chief for LA County and shared there are only 8 African
  American females out of 3300 firefighters. Also, attended the dinner for the Gardena
  Police Foundation for the annual golf tournament. Mayor Cerda commended the
  foundation for all the work they do. Mayor Cerda urged everyone to keep calling and using
  Gardena Direct to report illegal fireworks. Lastly, congratulate Mayor Pro Tem on his
  position of second vice president and wished Deputy City Clerk Becky a Happy Birthday.
  5. Council Member Francis – Council Member Francis wished Deputy City Clerk Becky a
  Happy Birthday. Council Member Francis thanked Mary Joy Coburn, Director of
  Communication from the greater Los Angeles Vector Control District for the presentation
  on mosquito awareness. Also thanked Lawanda Stanton and Diana for the excellent
  presentation on Human Services. Since the last meeting Council Member Francis
  attended the Community Safety Forum hosted by the Gardena Police Department and
  attended the Juneteenth celebration. Shared everyone missed Mayor Pro Tem Tanaka
  and Council Member Kaskanian. Council Member Francis shared Senator Steven
  Bradford told her the City of Gardena is getting a $2M grant to revitalize Gardena Blvd.
  She also shared a story when she became Council Member, Mr. Toyo who took her photo
  and all the council pictures once told her “Now that you’re on City Council what are you
  going to do for Gardena Blvd.” her answer to him was that it would be worked on so now
  she is very happy that it is finally happening. Council Member Francis encourage everyone
  to report illegal fireworks by calling the non-emergency phone number. Lastly, encouraged
